title: Exact-token probability response primitive
scope: A bounded native Arm64 validation of a source primitive that selects exact pre-sampling token probabilities from the same full softmax already computed by llama-server. It compares full-vocabulary and four-token response modes on one previously exposed E10a request shape. It is not an external holdout, a complete candidate-scoring endpoint, a cache policy, or an end-product performance claim.
hypothesis: On exact patched b10216 and the selected Ministral 3B Q4_K_M model, probability_ids returns A/B/C/D log probabilities equal to the existing full-vocabulary n_probs path within 1e-6 while reducing response bytes by at least 99% without increasing median HTTP latency by more than 5%.
negative_result_rule: Retain build failures, schema failures, probability mismatch, reordered or missing token IDs, response-size failure, latency regression, source-identity mismatch, or native mechanism failure without changing the prompt, token set, repetitions, tolerance, or promotion gates.

workload.calibration_source: The exact request shape already exposed by E10a; no independent task holdout is consumed.
workload.candidate_tokenization: Each candidate text must tokenize to exactly one token with add_special=false and parse_special=false.

execution.raw_response_retention: Every measured HTTP response is gzip-compressed and retained with compressed and uncompressed SHA-256 and byte count.

decision.promote_rule: Promote the exact-token response primitive for a separately frozen multi-token evaluator only if every validity, parity, response-size, and latency gate passes.
decision.stop_rule: If any gate fails, retain the native result and do not use the primitive for external quality claims.

claim_boundary: A passing E10b proves only that exact requested next-token log probabilities match the existing full-vocabulary server path and avoid its response payload on the tested native Arm service. It does not prove multi-token candidate scoring, prefix forking, lm-evaluation-harness compatibility, external-task quality, cache safety, energy, PMU, local-device, fleet, concurrency, cost, or other-runtime performance.
